correctness.rationale: For a singleton {s}, a successor v with false Δp must beat s and have outdegree at least two. At a failure root x, one has s≠x (the tournament has no opposite arcs) and x cannot beat s, since then Δp at x would force outdegree one. Thus s→x→v→s; the only cycles are j→i→k→j with i<k<j. For j<n, the later vertex j+1 supplies a successor with true Δp in each of the three cyclic roles. The distinct (s,x) pairs are (j,i), (i,k), (k,j), totaling 1+2(j−i−1) when the gap is at least two. For j=n, outdegree one at n rules out two roles, leaving (n,i), which fails exactly if x=i has both n−2 and n−1 as successors: the first beats n and n−1, the second beats only n. For all valuations the adjacent flips remain transitive, and in the terminal triangle each member has one successor while at earlier roots every successor's successor set is contained in the root's. This includes n=3 and gives n preserving labelled choices. The frozen VERIFICATION.md and check.py were inspected; a separate adjacency-set implementation agreed on all 119 reversals and 868 singleton assignments through n=9 and on validity over 11,256 Boolean assignments through n=8. That replay is bounded; the triangle proof covers arbitrary n. No Lean verification or specialist attestation is inferred.

value.rationale: A single changed arc is the first natural stability layer of transitivity. The lone cyclic preservation case separates modal validity from transitivity in that layer, and the exact singleton witness-pair profile distinguishes interior and terminal disruptions quantitatively. This is a reusable exact benchmark for tournament frame perturbations, not a claim about all tournaments or all countervaluations.
